# Canonical union of every apt package this repo's Linux jobs install.
#
# WHY A MANIFEST AND NOT JUST THE PER-CALL-SITE LISTS
#
# The nightly warmer (native-deps-freshness.yaml) is the ONLY writer of the .deb cache, and it
# runs on `main`, so its cache scope is the one every PR run can read from. A PR run writes only
# into its own `refs/pull/N/merge` scope, which no other PR can see (#352). That means the warmer
# has to download the packages OTHER jobs need, not just its own — before this file existed the
# warmer installed neither libclang-dev nor the mingw pair, so a PR job would have found them
# missing from an otherwise-warm cache and gone back to the mirror for exactly the ~35 MB that
# stalls most often.
#
# So: every package named at any call site of .github/actions/apt-install-cached belongs here.
# The action warns (loudly, in the job log) when it is asked for something this file does not
# list, because that package is silently uncached and is the next thing to delete a job.
#
# Cache key derives from a hash of this file, so editing it rotates the cache. The next nightly
# warmer run repopulates; PR runs in between just download as they did before. Degrades, never
# breaks.

# --- Host build deps for BoringSSL / quiche (cmake-configured, perl-driven) ---
build-essential
perl
pkg-config
cmake
nasm

# --- aarch64 cross toolchain ---
# The big one: g++-13-aarch64-linux-gnu (12.2 MB) + gcc-13-aarch64-linux-gnu (21.1 MB) are the two
# packages seen stalling at ~40 KB/s in both sightings on #368.
#
# libc6-dev-arm64-cross is named explicitly, not left to Recommends: it supplies
# /usr/aarch64-linux-gnu/include/sys/socket.h for the arm64 quiche_jni.c cross-compile, and as a
# mere *Recommends* of gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu it can silently not arrive (→ `fatal error:
# sys/socket.h: No such file`).
gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu
g++-aarch64-linux-gnu
libc6-dev-arm64-cross

# --- Windows cross toolchain (self-contained quiche build for windows-x64) ---
gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64
g++-mingw-w64-x86-64

# --- BoringSSL ASAN lane ---
# Its LLVM ASAN runtime must match cargo-fuzz's, so the lane installs clang rather than relying on
# the image's gcc. That step carries `continue-on-error: true`, which makes it look harmless — but
# continue-on-error does not survive the JOB timeout, so a stall there still deletes the lane
# exactly the way #368 describes, just without even a red step to point at.
clang

# --- bindgen ---
# quiche 0.29 dropped `boringssl-vendored`; the Windows/Android/fuzz builds use
# `boringssl-boring-crate`, whose boring-sys build script runs bindgen and needs libclang on the
# host. (Linux x64/arm64 use external BoringSSL + `ffi`, which needs no libclang.)
libclang-dev

# --- native-crash post-mortem ---
# build-linux.yaml's `if: failure()` gdb-backtrace steps (quiche-jvm, malloc-check, fuzz-jvm) load
# a core dump and print every thread's stack. Listing it here means a failed job's post-mortem no
# longer has to hit the mirror on the way down too — see apt-install-cached.
gdb
